FLASHCARD SET · AGES 3–4 YEARS

Color Flashcards for Preschoolers

Twelve color cards with two faces each: a big paint splash with the color word, and a matching picture from real life — a red apple, a blue car, a yellow sun. Name the color, find the picture, then go find the color in your house.

THE CARDS

Every card in the set.

Each card has its own page with the picture, the words to say and one thing to try together. Tap any card to open it.

RedCard 1 of 12BlueCard 2 of 12YellowCard 3 of 12GreenCard 4 of 12OrangeCard 5 of 12PurpleCard 6 of 12PinkCard 7 of 12BrownCard 8 of 12BlackCard 9 of 12WhiteCard 10 of 12GrayCard 11 of 12RainbowCard 12 of 12
HOW TO USE THESE CARDS

Four ways that work.

You do not need a plan or a printer schedule. Pick one idea, try it for two minutes and see what happens.

  1. 01

    One color a day is plenty

    Show the red splash in the morning, find red things all day, and let the set rest. A color that gets a whole day of spotting sticks far better than twelve colors in one sitting.

  2. 02

    Start from the splash, land on the picture

    Say the color at the splash — a pure, unmissable red — then move to the picture card, where the same color sits on a real thing. Splash first, world second, is the whole method.

  3. 03

    Let your child play the teacher

    Hand your child the cards and let them quiz YOU. Getting one wrong on purpose — “is this blue? no, it’s green!” — is the game three-year-olds never tire of.

  4. 04

    Give the color a home

    Tape today’s color card to the fridge at child height. Every trip past the fridge is one more quiet repetition, and repetitions — not sessions — are what make color words stick.
